headline: Fear-zone reading holds as yields grind higher into PCE
body: CNN's Fear & Greed gauge sits at 32 — still in Fear territory, just off Tuesday's 34 — after the Dow shed about 0.7% and the Nasdaq nearly 1% in a session dominated by another leg up in Treasury yields, with the 10-year near 5.2-5.3% (2007-era levels) and the 30-year above 5.5% (2004-era highs). The move follows this month's quarter-point Fed hike to 3.75-4.00%, the first since 2023, justified by core PCE inflation running above 3% all year. Wednesday's PCE print, expected to confirm a similar pace, is the next test of how much further the bond market's tightening bet runs. Futures firmed modestly into the release, and a fading government-shutdown risk — prediction markets now near 4% odds after funding progress — has taken one source of near-term tail anxiety off the table.

The more interesting split is inside the AI trade. OpenAI halting training and shelving its next flagship model after internal safety failures rattled sentiment around AI infrastructure names already sensitive to higher long-end yields. Retail chatter tracked from Reddit's WallStreetBets hasn't caught the same unease, though: Nvidia, Micron, and Meta remain the most-discussed tickers with a bullish lean, and mentions of Tesla and SpaceX have spiked sharply in the past day. AMD's $8.2 billion purchase of AI startup World Labs, met with a modest share gain, suggests deal-making appetite for AI infrastructure hasn't cooled even as the macro backdrop turns more cautious. Bond-market wariness against still-eager retail positioning in the same handful of AI names looks like today's more telling tension than any single index move.
